title: Peripheral artery disease: stage, side and ulcer
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's peripheral artery disease and any related ulcer.
note:
Chief Complaint
Leg pain.

HPI
The patient is an 89-year-old woman presenting for a follow-up evaluation of chronic pain. She reports significant rest pain in the left foot. She notes that the symptoms are localized specifically to the left lower extremity and have been persistent. She denies any new skin breakdown or drainage.

Medication List
Lisinopril 10mg daily
Atorvastatin 40mg daily
Aspirin 81mg daily

Exam
The patient is alert and oriented. Physical examination reveals decreased pulses in the left leg. There is palpable atherosclerosis of the native leg arteries. The skin is intact with no signs of break in the skin or drainage. The left foot shows some coolness compared to the rest of the body.

Assessment
1. Atherosclerosis of the native leg arteries, affecting only the left leg.
2. Rest pain in the left foot.

Plan
1. Continue current antiplatelet and lipid-lowering medications.
2. Monitor symptoms of rest pain.
3. Schedule a follow-up and repeat vascular imaging in three months to monitor the progression of atherosclerosis.

Electronically signed, P. O'Brien, MD
May 14, 2026
explanations: Atherosclerosis of native arteries of the left leg with rest pain (HCC 264): I70.222.

distractors.why: Rest pain is documented: it is a higher stage (HCC 264).
